subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Does any current browser-reachable, state-changing Gateway HTTP route bypass the existing origin policy under a supported authentication mode?
rationale: Closing requires security-owner confirmation that the documented origin gate covers every relevant route; changing the shared gate without that inventory could either leave a bypass or break supported non-browser clients.

options.title: Verify route coverage
options.body: Run a controlled route and authentication-mode audit, closing this issue if all browser-origin state-changing requests are already rejected as documented.

options.title: Harden shared HTTP auth
options.body: If a bypass is reproduced, enforce the existing origin policy before authentication or dispatch at the common Gateway HTTP boundary and add regression coverage.

options.title: Adopt CSRF tokens
options.body: Introduce a separate anti-CSRF token only if an ambient browser credential mode remains vulnerable after origin enforcement and its compatibility impact is approved.

recommendation.title: Verify route coverage
recommendation.body: Run a controlled route and authentication-mode audit, closing this issue if all browser-origin state-changing requests are already rejected as documented.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work is the strongest available history signal for Gateway HTTP authentication and scope boundaries.
